notes.title: Family System, National Leaders, Civil War System, Religion Editor and RTS
notes.notes: [h1]1. Family System and National Leaders[/h1][p]Each country now has different families, and based on their political system, countries have leaders with different titles.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45133465/d3e74ac3e5915825b059596029d779e54dbd09ce.png"][/img][/p][p]Leader Titles by Political System:[/p][p]- Kingdom: King/Queen[/p][p]- Empire: Emperor/Empress[/p][p]- Republic: Consul[/p][p]- Federation: Grand Consul[/p][p]- Tribal: Chief[/p][p]- Theocracy: Pope[/p][h1]2. Character System[/h1][p]Characters have four core attributes:[/p][p]- Charisma: Affects diplomatic ability and public support[/p][p]- Military: Affects army combat effectiveness and war command ability[/p][p]- Diplomatic: Affects diplomatic negotiations and international relations[/p][p]- Administrative: Affects national management efficiency and tax collection[/p][p]Character Trait System:[/p][p]- Traits modify the four attributes, e.g., "Genius" trait significantly boosts administrative ability[/p][p]- Some traits are mutually exclusive, e.g., "Kind" and "Cruel" cannot coexist[/p][p]- Special traits like "Reformer" may trigger political reforms upon taking office[/p][p]- Leader traits also affect the nation as a whole, such as tax efficiency and rebellion resistance[/p][h1]3. Family Tree[/h1][p]You can view a family's family tree page by clicking in Family Panel -> Behaviors. It displays the family members in a tree structure.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45133465/56515c290f43083cd38632b8734c2aee58559ecb.png"][/img][/p][h1]4. Civil War System[/h1][p][/p][p]Civil War Trigger Conditions:[/p][p]- Country must have at least 10 provinces for civil war to occur[/p][p]- Must be at least 36 months since last civil war[/p][p]- Civil wars more likely when country is corrupted[/p][p]- Triggered when family influence and dissatisfaction reach certain thresholds[/p][p]Civil War Types:[/p][p]- Succession: Other families claim succession rights to the throne[/p][p]- Reform: Family attempts to change the political system[/p][p]- Independence: Family attempts to split and become independent[/p][p]- Overthrow: Family attempts to overthrow the current ruler[/p][p]- Family Rebellion: Dissatisfied family directly rebels[/p][p]Civil War Mechanics:[/p][p]- Rebels gain support from provinces based on family influence[/p][p]- During civil war, the original country splits into two opposing forces[/p][p]- The losing side is annexed, the winner inherits the country[/p][p]- Successful reform civil wars change the political system[/p][p]- Successful family rebellions may establish new independent nations[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45133465/b3c529555f9cbedec3e431ea8df3806bb0e9c621.png"][/img][/p][h1]5. Separate Country History Timeline[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45133465/d3e74ac3e5915825b059596029d779e54dbd09ce.png"][/img][/p][p]New History Event Types in Timeline System:[/p][p]Leader-Related Events:[/p][p]- Leader Ascension: Records new leaders taking power through inheritance, election, or coup[/p][p]- Leader Death: Records leader deaths[/p][p]- Leader Abdication: Records voluntary abdications[/p][p]- Election Held: Regular elections in republican countries[/p][p]- Reform: Records major political system changes[/p][p]Family-Related Events:[/p][p]- Family Founded: Birth of new noble families[/p][p]- Family Extinct: Family line dies out[/p][p]- Family Rise: Family becomes ruling family[/p][p]- Family Rebellion: Family launches rebellion[/p][p]- Family Swear Fealty: Defeated family swears allegiance[/p][p]- Family Exile: Family is driven into exile[/p][p]- Family Purged: Family is completely eliminated[/p][p]Civil War and Rebellion Events:[/p][p]- Civil War Start: Records civil war outbreak[/p][p]- Civil War End: Records civil war outcome[/p][p]- Rebellion Succeeded/Suppressed: Records outcomes of various rebellions[/p][p]Other New Events:[/p][p]- Province Granted: Provinces awarded to families[/p][p]- Province Revoked: Family lands reclaimed[/p][p]- Family Rally: Family initiates or responds to rallies[/p][h1]6. Religion View and Religion Editor[/h1][p]Religion System Features:[/p][p]- Religion View Mode: Switch to religion view to see distribution and influence of religions[/p][p]- Religion Information Panel: Displays basic information about religions and religion sets[/p][p]- Religion Editing Features:[/p][p]  - Edit religion name, description, and holy book[/p][p]  - Set religion representative color[/p][p]  - Designate holy provinces[/p][p]- Religion Set Management:[/p][p]  - Create and manage religion sets (religion collections)[/p][p]  - Import/export religion configurations[/p][p]  - Multi-language translation support[/p][p]- Workshop Support: Upload and download religion sets to Steam Workshop[/p][h1]7. Real-Time Strategy Mode (BETA)[/h1][p]Real-Time Strategy mode allows players to directly control a country's armies:[/p][p]How to Enable:[/p][p]- Click "Enable RTS Mode" button in State Panel -> Behavior[/p][p]- Can only control one country's armies at a time[/p][p]Controls:[/p][p]- Mouse Box Select: Drag to select multiple armies[/p][p]- Right Click: Command selected armies to move to target location[/p][p]- ESC Key: Exit RTS mode[/p]

notes.title: Culture View and New Editor UI
notes.notes:
[h2]Culture View, Alliance View, a new Editor UI[/h2]

[h3]views[/h3]

Press 1, 2, 3 to switch between Country, Alliance, and Culture views.

[h3]Culture[/h3]

The Culture system includes regions where countries can emerge or rebel. The probability of a country's traits, ethnic attributes, and political system appearing is determined by weight values.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45133465/2a6f6a6c899917e320ea12564506809f10d34233.png[/img]

[h3]Editor UI[/h3]

The UI for map editing has been remade. Currently, the Country Panel, Culture Panel, and Map Editing UIs are new versions. Other UIs will be remade successively in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45133465/17da1318673cbef05cd47efa2c95a56a44ecdca6.png[/img]

[h3]Translation[/h3]

A built-in Microsoft translation function is now available for translating countries, cultures, and provinces. Global translation can also be performed in Map Editing -> Global Commands.

[h3]Future Update Plan[/h3]

The Alliance Panel, Religion Panel, and Religion View will be implemented soon. 

If development goes smoothly, the first major system update will be launched in September: National Leaders and the Family System. Stay tuned!

notes.title: Editor Improvements Update Notes - January 16
notes.notes:
[h2]I. Editor Logic Improvements[/h2]    [list]        [*]When switching to different editing options, the corresponding view will now automatically switch without needing to adjust administrative map transparency or background map type in map appearance settings. After closing the editing panel, the map will revert to display according to map appearance settings.[/*]    [/list]    [h2]II. Province Editing Features Update[/h2]    [list]        [*]Added a regenerate province button and average province cell count option in the province editing panel. You can adjust province generation density by modifying the average number of cells per province.[/*]    [/list]    [h2]III. Interface Tooltip Improvements[/h2]    [list]        [*]Added numerous editor-related tooltips. Hover your mouse over buttons to see their usage instructions.[/*]    [/list]    [h2]IV. New Map Editing Tutorial[/h2]    
1. Map Mechanics: Based on Voronoi diagrams, each province consists of multiple adjacent polygons (cells). A province is the smallest unit that a country can occupy. Therefore, provinces need to be edited before countries.
    
2. Editing Sequence:
    [list]        [*]Open the global command panel and disable autonomous diplomacy and rebellion to prevent countries from attacking each other or engaging in diplomatic actions and rebellions.[/*]        [*]Generate a height map, which can be edited using the brush tool.[/*]        [*]Generate a biome map based on the height map, which can be edited using the brush tool. You can also adjust ecological parameters to automatically generate biomes.[/*]        [*]Generate a province map based on the biome map, which can be edited using the brush tool.[/*]        [*]Generate a country map based on the province map, or place countries to occupy each province.[/*]        [*]Enable autonomous diplomacy and rebellion to start the game.[/*]    [/list]    
3. To modify country attributes such as religion or government type, left-click on the corresponding country on the map to open the country information panel for editing.
    
4. To change province names or categories, shift + left-click on the corresponding province on the map to open the province information panel for editing.
    [h2]V. Multilingual Support Optimization[/h2]    [list]        [*]Fixed Chinese character display issues for Latin-based languages and Korean. Maps with Chinese and Japanese text downloaded from the Workshop will now display correctly without showing squares. Built-in translation features will be added in the future to facilitate map sharing among players of different languages.[/*]    [/list]    [h2]VI. Performance Optimization[/h2]    [list]        [*]Fixed lag issues caused by excessive alliances in certain situations.[/*]    [/list]    [h2]VII. Bug Fixes and Feature Updates[/h2]    [list]        [*]Fixed an issue where regenerating ecology would clear rivers and prevent refreshing the ecology map.[/*]        [*]Added a new global command option: toggle generation of unconquerable regions in tundra and desert. You can disable this option if you don't want these region types to generate.[/*]    [/list]

notes.title: New Steam grand strategy game puts the focus on the very map itself
notes.notes:
When was the last time you actually thought about a videogame map? We use them all the time in open-world, Metroidvania, and strategy games, but they almost always fly under the radar. That's what a good map does though; it goes unnoticed. Diagetic maps like those found in Metro Exodus and Far Cry 2 stand out because they exist within the character's world as well as yours, but they aren't always the best. The cream of the topographical crop marries art style, functionality, and mechanics in a way that makes a map unforgettable, and not many games can boast that staying power. In walks Fantasy Map Simulator. It's all maps all the time, and it looks absolutely gorgeous.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.notes:
[h1]Update Log[/h1]

New Features
- Added the function to delete saved games

Interface Improvements
- Separated the pause button from the speed adjustment feature

Bug Fixes
- Fixed an issue where continuing the game during historical playback would cause map distortion
- Resolved a problem where armies were abnormally large in certain situations

notes.title: Small Update
notes.notes:
New Features:
- Music volume settings can now be saved in the game configuration file

Bug Fixes:
- Fixed an issue where province names were displayed incorrectly after placing a country

notes.title: Workshop Related Bugs Fix
notes.notes: Now you can subscribe to and upload maps, religions, and culture sets to the Workshop. Subscribed maps, religions, and culture sets can be automatically loaded into the game. Maps can be found in the loading saves

notes.title: Fantasy Map Simulator EA Release Note !
notes.notes:
[h1]Official Version Update Log:[/h1] [list] [*]The Workshop is now open, allowing uploads of maps, custom religions, and culture sets. National attributes, specialties, and localization files can be edited and tested locally. Please remember to back up your files, as game updates may delete your custom mods.[/*] [*]Added volume control functionality, allowing players to adjust the volume.[/*] [*]Added current campaign information for provinces, allowing players to view the progress of provincial campaigns.[/*] [*]Added more documentation.[/*] [*]Removed the 700-year game time limit. Theoretically, game time is now unlimited, but extremely long game times (tens of thousands of years) may result in large save files (due to the historical backtracking feature), leading to longer save and load times.[/*] [*]Fixed some localization issues across various languages.[/*] [*]Added army camera follow functionality.[/*] [*]Added random appearance display and 8 map appearance templates for players to choose from.[/*] [*]Added a national editing panel, allowing editing of national attributes, government systems, religions, and ethnic attributes.[/*] [*]Added in-game plans for future updates, please check for details.[/*] [/list] [h2]AI has undergone some overall adjustments. The main mechanisms of the latest game are explained as follows:[/h2] [olist] [*]Corruption Mechanism [list] [*]After a nation is established, corruption values gradually increase over time[/*] [*]The accumulation speed of corruption is affected by the following factors: [list] [*]Population: When the population is too high (falling into the Malthusian trap), corruption accumulates faster[/*] [*]Economy: When the treasury is in deficit, corruption accumulates faster[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]When corruption is too high, it will trigger a potential background reform event (currently without event text), which will reset the corruption value[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]Population System [list] [*]Provincial population cap is based on the current biome[/*] [*]Population growth rate is affected by ethnic attributes[/*] [*]War leads to population decline[/*] [*]Low population reduces the willingness to initiate wars[/*] [*]Population size determines troop replenishment rate[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]Economy and Specialty System [list] [*]Provincial resources are determined by the biome[/*] [*]Economic output is affected by ethnic attributes and national government system[/*] [*]Military expenses depend on troop mobilization[/*] [*]Administrative efficiency is determined by the size of the territory[/*] [*]Taxation is based on population and specialties[/*] [*]War reduces the economic output of the affected province to zero[/*] [*]Corruption affects tax efficiency[/*] [*]Treasury deficit reduces the willingness to initiate wars[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]Core Area [list] [*]Centered around the capital, expands over time[/*] [*]Emergency mobilization when threatened[/*] [*]Mobilization scale is affected by corruption level and economic status[/*] [*]Leaves national ethnic imprints, deeper with longer time[/*] [*]Clears the ethnic imprints of extinct nations[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]Rebellion and Nation Restoration System [list] [*]The farther from the core area, the higher the probability of rebellion[/*] [*]Remote areas are prone to rebellion during high corruption[/*] [*]Rebellion may lead to the restoration of old nations in that province[/*] [*]Even core areas may rebel under extreme corruption[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]Combat System [list] [*]Army combat effectiveness is affected by terrain, economy, corruption level, and national characteristics[/*] [*]Interior operations (core area) have easy supply lines and lower military expenses[/*] [*]Expeditions or overseas operations are costly, with high military expenses[/*] [*]Surrounded or semi-surrounded troops are in a "salient", with halved combat effectiveness[/*] [*]Island nation strategy: May conduct frequent harassing attacks against continental nations [list] [*]May cause continental nations' armies to be constantly on the move[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]Only maritime and commercial ethnicities or very powerful nations will conduct distant overseas operations[/*] [*]Armies will prioritize deployment at borders[/*] [*]Armies are divided into potential garrison troops, guard troops, and field troops [list] [*]Field armies prioritize attacking foreign territories[/*] [*]Guard troops prioritize suppressing rebellions[/*] [*]Garrison troops prioritize stationing[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]When the capital is threatened (nearby provinces are attacked), the national army's troop efficiency will increase by one level, and some garrison troops will change their identity[/*] [*]Fortresses: Will build fortresses or checkpoints in mountainous areas, which are difficult to conquer[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]Diplomatic System

Basic Relations Between Government Systems

[h3]Republic Federation (Republic)[/h3] [list] [*]Most friendly with republics and federations[/*] [*]Good relations with kingdoms[/*] [*]Slightly tense relations with tribal systems[/*] [*]Most opposed to empires and theocracies[/*] [/list] [h3]Empire[/h3] [list] [*]Closest relations with kingdoms[/*] [*]Neutral towards tribal systems and theocracies[/*] [*]Tense relations with republics and federations[/*] [*]Strong competitive relationships with other empires[/*] [/list] [h3]Kingdom[/h3] [list] [*]Good relations with republics, federations, and other kingdoms[/*] [*]Slightly better relations with theocracies[/*] [*]Neutral towards tribal systems[/*] [*]Slightly tense relations with empires[/*] [/list] [h3]Tribal[/h3] [list] [*]Closest relations with other tribal systems[/*] [*]Neutral towards kingdoms and theocracies[/*] [*]Relatively tense relations with republics, federations, and empires[/*] [/list] [h3]Theocracy[/h3] [list] [*]Good relations with kingdoms[/*] [*]Neutral towards tribal systems[/*] [*]Relatively tense relations with republics, federations, and empires[/*] [*]Potential conflicts with other theocracies[/*] [*]Special ability: Strong religious propagation ability, may influence other nations[/*] [/list]

National Strength and Diplomatic Attitude

[olist] [*]Great Power Effect: [list] [*]When a nation becomes too powerful, all other nations' diplomatic attitudes towards it will deteriorate[/*] [/list] [/*] [*]Corruption and War Risk: [list] [*]If a powerful nation also has severe corruption problems, other nations may see it as an opportunity[/*] [*]In this case, the likelihood of other nations declaring war on this seemingly strong but internally corrupt nation increases[/*] [/list] [/*] [/olist]

Dynamic Diplomatic Relations

[list] [*]Initial diplomatic relations are based on government types but will change as the game progresses[/*] [*]Influencing factors include: common enemies, historical events, national strength comparison, internal corruption levels, etc.[/*] [*]For theocracies, their ability to convert religions is stronger[/*] [*]If some nations in an alliance become too powerful, the current alliance will dissolve[/*] [/list]

Randomness

[list] [*]All the above systems are not absolute, there are some random factors to simulate low-probability events. However, the general trend is as described above.[/*] [/list] [/*] [/olist]
